articles.author: Molly Taft, WIRED
articles.summary: Roughly 160 people are dead and hundreds more — including dozens of international tourists — are missing after flash floods hit a region on the mountainous border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday. Devastating footage posted to social media shows people fleeing a wall of water that washed away buildings and vehicles. Initial analysis of satellite imagery and reports from the Nepalese government indicate that the flooding was likely triggered by a landslide caused after a piece of a glacier fell hundreds of feet. As the region warms, its ice is becoming increasingly unstable , raising the risk of catastrophic flooding. “The glaciers over there are definitely in retreat,” said Joseph Shea, an associate professor of geography at the University of Northern British Columbia. “There’s a lot of glacier mass up there, but we’re seeing thinning, we’re seeing retreating.” Since 2000, the world’s glaciers have lost 5 percent of their ice , with much more drastic impacts in certain regions. Nepal’s glaciers lost nearly a quarter of their area between 1970 and 2010. More than 160 smaller glaciers in the country, research has found, have vanished entirely. Under the agreement, a joint company comprising the US government and a Venezuelan private operator will receive a 100-year lease to develop 17 oil fields. Venezuela’s acting president said the agreement could draw billions in investment, but critics across Venezuela’s political spectrum questioned its legality and warned it could undermine Venezuelan sovereignty. articles.summary: US President Donald Trump announced Friday that the US had secured majority control over more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves, expanding Washington’s influence over the country’s energy industry. Under the agreement, a joint company comprising the US government and a Venezuelan private operator will receive a 100-year lease to develop 17 oil fields. Venezuela’s acting president said the agreement could draw billions in investment, but critics across Venezuela’s political spectrum questioned its legality and warned it could undermine Venezuelan sovereignty. The deal marked a win for Trump, who has urged American oil companies to return to Venezuela since Nicolás Maduro’s ouster; after months of hesitation, Chevron and others are now nearing billion-dollar deals , The Wall Street Journal reported. — Lauren Morganbesser

articles.summary: Anthropic temporarily paused some AI training and cybersecurity evaluations, the company said in a blog post today detailing changes made after unauthorized actions by its agents earlier this year. Why it matters: Rival OpenAI said it had paused some model work due to safety concerns. Now, we know Anthropic did the same — and they're reiterating the need for a broader pacing of frontier AI development. Driving the news: Anthropic said it paused external cyber evaluations of pre-release models after three incidents it disclosed in July, and also briefly paused its own in-house tests of pre-release models. The company also paused higher-risk reinforcement-learning environments on pre-release models for several weeks after the incidents. Zoom in: Most reinforcement learning has resumed, but some high-risk environments remain paused pending manual review or updated monitoring tools, according to Anthropic's blog post . articles.summary: I spent a night at the Madonna Inn, a delirious confection of a hotel in San Luis Obispo, a few years ago with my family. The in-house restaurant there—properly called Alex Madonna’s Gold Rush Steak House—has round pink padded booths accented with gold, a riot of artificial flowers festooning the crystal chandeliers, and dizzying pink carpet patterned with huge roses. I visit this place every chance I get. To sit in one of those booths in a velvet dress and eat a huge slab of pink champagne cake is the closest I have ever come in this life to total bliss. On the night in question I joined my husband, his sister and his dad in a particularly magnificent booth: it was slightly set back from the main room, under a huge mirror, and padded in all gold instead of the usual pink. Returning to the table and seeing my dazed, euphoric expression, our waitress smiled, leaned over and said, so only I could hear: “You’re sitting in Dolly’s seat.” Joe Mabel [CC BY-SA 4.0] via Wikimedia Commons Motel Madonna Inn San Luis Obispo California. articles.summary: Dolly Parton was 32 when she posed for the cover of Playboy in 1978 , wearing a rhinestone and sequins version of the Playboy bunny costume. After some probing questions about her style and “gaudy getup,” interviewer Lawrence Grobel began asking whether her husband Carl Dean was a “jealous person.” (She swore he was not.) The idea seemed to fascinate journalists of the day, including Grobel, who followed up by asking whether Dolly herself was the jealous type or whether either spouse dated other people while she was on the road. (Though she kept the details of their personal life fairly vague, she answered that she was not, they did not.) The line of questioning continued for some time, beyond the point when she warned Grobel that he was asking very personal questions of a very private person, until finally he asked whether sleeping with other people could “lead to complications” in her life. “Well,” Dolly replied, “kiss me, we’ll see.”
